text: Eliminative materialism, as defended by the Churchlands, holds that folk psychology (belief, desire, and the rest) is:
choices: A true theory that reduces smoothly to neuroscience
A radically false theory whose posits will be eliminated — not reduced — by a mature neuroscience
A useful fiction that is nonetheless literally true of immaterial minds
Identical in meaning to neuroscientific vocabulary
explanation: The Churchlands argue folk psychology is a false empirical theory whose entities (like phlogiston) will be replaced, not reduced, by neuroscience — they simply do not refer. Option 0 describes reductive physicalism; option 3 describes an analytic reduction they reject; option 2 is a dualist/fictionalist reading. Elimination is defined precisely by contrast with reduction.
